newsitem.title: UK: Britain welcomes Iraq oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: Britain welcomes Iraq oil-for-food deal.

text.p: Britain on Tuesday welcomed Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations but said it was unlikely all sanctions against Baghdad would be lifted while Saddam Hussein remained in power.

On Monday, Iraq's U.N. ambassador said he had given the U.N. a letter setting out "the official Iraqi acceptance" of the terms for the deal, which would allow Baghdad to sell oil in international markets for the first time in six years.
Iraq has been under sanctions since it invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
"We are pleased that Iraq has finally agreed to the implementation of Security Council Resolution 986, as we have long urged," a British Foreign Office spokesman said in a statement.
Noting that the agreement had been pending since May, the spokesman said: "Saddam's delay has caused much unnecessary suffering to the Iraqi people.

"Implementation will bring them some relief, but they will sadly not enjoy a normal life until Iraq fulfils its obligations under the relevant U.N. Security Council resolutions. Sanctions will remain until Iraq does so. It is hard to imagine this happening while Saddam remains in power."
Food prices plunged in Iraq on Tuesday after news of the deal, which will allow Iraq to sell $2 billion of crude oil over six months to buy food and medicines.
